changes.before: Inflation on a 12‑month basis is expected to remain somewhat below 2 percent in the near term but to stabilize around the Committee's 2 percent objective over the medium term.
changes.after: Inflation on a 12‑month basis is expected to move up this year and to stabilize around the Committee's 2 percent objective over the medium term.

changes.before: The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant gradual increases in the federal funds rate;
changes.after: The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant further gradual increases in the federal funds rate;

changes.before: Consequently, the Committee continues to expect that, with gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy,
changes.after: The Committee expects that, with further gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy,

changes.before: Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low;
changes.after: Market-based measures of inflation compensation have increased in recent months but remain low;

changes.before: Averaging through hurricane-related fluctuations, job gains have been solid, and the unemployment rate declined further. Household spending has been expanding at a moderate rate, and growth in business fixed investment has picked up in recent quarters.
changes.after: Gains in employment, household spending, and business fixed investment have been solid, and the unemployment rate has stayed low.

changes.before: the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/4 to 1‑1/2 percent.
changes.after: the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-1/4 to 1‑1/2 percent.

changes.before: Voting against the action were Charles L. Evans and Neel Kashkari, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the existing target range for the federal funds rate.

parsed.rationale: Although rates were held, the statement upgraded the inflation outlook (expected to move up this year), noted rising inflation compensation, and added 'further' to the gradual-increase guidance, signaling continued tightening. These are incremental hawkish tweaks rather than a change in policy direction.

spans.quote: Inflation on a 12‑month basis is expected to remain somewhat below 2 percent in the near term but to stabilize around the Committee's 2 percent objective over the medium term.
The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant gradual increases in the federal funds rate;
Consequently, the Committee continues to expect that, with gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy,
Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low;

Averaging through hurricane-related fluctuations, job gains have been solid, and the unemployment rate declined further. Household spending has been expanding at a moderate rate, and growth in business fixed investment has picked up in recent quarters.
the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/4 to 1‑1/2 percent.
Voting against the action were Charles L. Evans and Neel Kashkari, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the existing target range for the federal funds rate.
Inflation on a 12‑month basis is expected to move up this year and to stabilize around the Committee's 2 percent objective over the medium term.
The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant further gradual increases in the federal funds rate;
The Committee expects that, with further gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy,
Market-based measures of inflation compensation have increased in recent months but remain low;
Gains in employment, household spending, and business fixed investment have been solid, and the unemployment rate has stayed low.
the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-1/4 to 1‑1/2 percent.
